newsitem.title: NORWAY: Amoco, Conoco in Norway oil assets deal.
newsitem.headline: Amoco, Conoco in Norway oil assets deal.

text.p: Amoco Norway Oil Co said on Tuesday it had acquired additional stakes in the North Sea Ula and Gyda oilfields from Norske Conoco AS.
Amoco said it had bought Conoco's 10 percent interest in Ula and 9.375 percent in Gyda, both operated by British Petroleum Co Plc, and Conoco's 10 percent share in the adjoining licence PL164.
As part of the agreement, Conoco will take a 20 percent stake in licence PL011. Amoco will retain its 30 percent interest in PL011 and Norske Shell 50 percent.
Amoco now holds a 15 percent interest in the Ula field and 13.375 percent in Gyda.

"We have been actively building our exploration portfolio in this area," said Amoco Norway General Manager Anders Moerland. "This transaction will allow further consolidation and harmonisation of our position in the area and is aligned with our strategy to improve near-term profitability while providing opportunities for long-term growth."

Mike Johnson, President and Managing Director at Norske Conoco, said Ula and Gyda represented less than six percent of the company's current production and less than three percent of reserves and value.

"They have been profitable fields over the years, but no longer fit our long-term growth strategy," Johnson said. "The exploration potential in PL011 represents the type of newer generation assets we need to focus on for securing our long-term future and growth in Norway."
